assistant|peace_lily_light: peace lilies prefer bright, indirect light; direct sun can scorch leaves, and east- or west-facing windows are ideal

assistant|peace_lily_pruning: remove dead or dying leaves and flowers with clean, sharp scissors to prevent disease spread
assistant|peace_lily_repotting: repot in spring or summer if outgrown, using a slightly larger pot and fresh potting mix
assistant|peace_lily_pests: check regularly for spider mites, mealybugs, or scale; treat with insecticidal soap or neem oil
assistant|succulent_care: succulents have different care requirements than peace lilies; research species-specific water, light, and nutrient needs
assistant|fertilizer_routine: options: continue the nursery mixture as directed, switch to a balanced 20-20-20 fertilizer, or dilute to half strength; over-fertilizing is more harmful than under-fertilizing
assistant|fern_humidity: ferns thrive in very humid conditions, often above 50% relative humidity, while peace lilies tolerate around 40-50%
assistant|peace_lily_misting: mist peace lilies 1-2 times per week in average conditions, or every 3-4 days in dry environments; mist in the morning with room-temperature water, avoiding the crown
assistant|watering_frequency: water the peace lily when the top 1-2 inches of soil feel dry: roughly every 7-10 days in spring/summer and every 10-14 days in fall/winter
assistant|fertilizer_frequency: fertilize the peace lily every 1-2 weeks during the growing season (spring/summer) and once a month during dormancy (fall/winter)
assistant|rose_pruning: deadhead spent rose flowers anytime; light shaping pruning is OK now, but extensive pruning should wait until the blooming season is over
assistant|rose_pruning_timing: for most rose varieties the best time to prune is the dormant season (winter or early spring); make clean 45-degree cuts and remove weak or diseased wood

assistant|basil_light_advice: Basil thrives in partial shade; move to a spot with indirect sunlight or use a sheer curtain/shade cloth
assistant|basil_watering_advice: Basil in shadier spots needs less water; check soil moisture to the first knuckle and water only when dry
assistant|basil_humidity_advice: Basil loves humid environments; use a tray of water and pebbles or a humidifier to maintain humidity
assistant|basil_fertilizer_advice: Feed basil with balanced water-soluble fertilizer at half the recommended strength; overfertilization is detrimental
assistant|basil_pruning_advice: Pinch off basil flower buds to encourage leaf growth and trim leggy stems to keep a bushy shape
assistant|basil_temperature_advice: Basil prefers daytime temperatures between 65-75°F (18-24°C); avoid drafty areas and extreme temperature fluctuations
assistant|basil_soil_drainage_advice: Basil needs well-draining soil with perlite, vermiculite, or sand to prevent waterlogging and root rot
assistant|basil_soil_ph_advice: Basil prefers slightly acidic to neutral soil pH ranging from 6.0 to 7.0
assistant|basil_soil_organic_advice: Basil loves soil rich in organic matter such as compost or peat moss for moisture, temperature regulation, and nutrients
assistant|basil_potting_mix_recipe: DIY basil potting mix: 2 parts peat moss or coconut coir, 1 part perlite or vermiculite, 1 part compost or worm castings, 1 part general-purpose potting soil
assistant|snake_plant: Repot a snake plant when root-bound, soil depleted, or visibly grown; choose a pot only 1-2 sizes larger since they prefer being slightly root-bound
assistant|snake_plant_repot_timing_advic: Repot snake plants during spring or summer when the plant is actively growing
assistant|fern_pest_identification: The tiny moving dots on the fern are likely spider mites or springtails; spider mites feed on sap and may leave webbing, springtails are harmless to plants
assistant|fern_pest_control_methods: Organic pest control for ferns: neem oil, soap solution, insecticidal soap, horticultural oil; also isolate the plant, prune infested areas, improve air circulation
assistant|fern_misting: Mist fern 2-3 times per week with distilled or filtered water in the morning; ferns prefer 40-60% relative humidity; avoid getting water on the crown
Suggested approach for fern: treat with neem oil, wait a few days, then mist 2-3 times a week to prevent pests returning
